Lightweight version information struct for the Oboe library. Provides compile-time constants for major, minor, and patch numbers, a text representation, and a monotonically increasing integer encoding. No instances are typically created; members are static constants.

Abstract base class in namespace oboe that encapsulates configuration parameters and callbacks common to audio streams and their builders. It stores format, sample rate, channel configuration, sharing/performance modes, device IDs, policy flags, and callback pointers/shared_ptrs. Provides trivial ctor/dtor, default copy/assign, numerous getters, and a virtual isValidConfig plus small virtual buffer getters to be overridden by concrete stream implementations. Construction is via normal C++ new or by derived builder classes; no factory in this header.

Interface class for real-time audio data processing callbacks used with AudioStreamBuilder::setDataCallback(). Implement onAudioReady to supply or consume numFrames of audio via the provided buffer without calling read/write on the stream. Must adhere to real-time constraints (no blocking, allocation, I/O, or locks). Return DataCallbackResult::Continue or ::Stop. Details about DataCallbackResult and AudioStream are defined elsewhere.

Interface class for receiving stream error/disconnection notifications via methods invoked on an Oboe-managed thread. Use with AudioStreamBuilder::setErrorCallback(). Implement onError to optionally handle stop/close yourself (return true) or let Oboe handle it (return false) and receive onErrorBeforeClose and onErrorAfterClose. Do not close/delete the stream inside onErrorBeforeClose.
Interface class for offload presentation events. Notifies when all queued audio buffers in the system have finished playing. Use with AudioStreamBuilder::setPresentationCallback().

Interface class for partial data processing callbacks used with AudioStreamBuilder::setPartialDataCallback(). Allows processing fewer than numFrames and returning the actual frame count processed. Subject to real-time constraints. Note: Android supports partial data callbacks via AAudio starting API level 37; otherwise clients should process all requested frames. Returning a negative value stops the stream.

Deprecated combined callback interface that inherits both AudioStreamDataCallback and AudioStreamErrorCallback. Previously used with AudioStreamBuilder::setCallback(); prefer setting the data and error callbacks separately.

objects.definition: struct StreamDeleterFunctor;
objects.description: Forward declaration of a custom deleter functor used with ManagedStream unique_ptr to properly close and delete an AudioStream. Only declared here; the definition and behavior are not provided in this header.

objects.definition: using ManagedStream = std::unique_ptr<AudioStream, StreamDeleterFunctor>;
objects.description: Type alias for a unique_ptr managing an oboe::AudioStream with a custom deleter (StreamDeleterFunctor). When a ManagedStream goes out of scope, the deleter will close and delete the stream. Construction is via std::unique_ptr semantics; this alias itself does not define construction behavior beyond unique_ptr.

Factory/builder class for configuring and opening oboe::AudioStream instances. Inherits from AudioStreamBase and exposes a fluent API to set parameters such as channel count/mask, direction, sample rate, format, buffer capacity, sharing/performance modes, usage/content type, input preset, session id, device selection, capture/privacy/spatialization policies, callbacks, and conversion allowances. Provides openStream methods that create/open streams and optionally wrap them in shared_ptr or ManagedStream. Static helpers indicate AAudio availability/recommendation. Destruction and lifetime are managed by users or via smart pointer wrappers; this header does not include destructor details.

objects.definition: constexpr int64_t kDefaultTimeoutNanos = (2000 * kNanosPerMillisecond);
objects.description: Constant timeout in nanoseconds used as the default for blocking state-change operations on an Oboe AudioStream. Pointer type shown as required by schema; this is a scalar constant, not heap-allocated.

Primary Oboe C++ audio stream abstraction. Provides synchronous and asynchronous control (start/stop/pause/flush), I/O (read/write), timestamping/latency utilities, performance hinting, and counters. It is abstract; platform-specific subclasses implement the pure virtual methods and low-level interaction with audio backends. Lifecycle: construct via AudioStreamBuilder (external), open(), start()/stop(), close(). Thread-safe operations guarded by internal mutex for start/stop/close. Contains callback swapping utilities and performance hint hooks. Some methods may return ErrorUnimplemented depending on backend support.
Stateless functor intended as a custom deleter for smart pointers to oboe::AudioStream. Ensures the stream is closed before deletion to release audio resources safely.

A utility class that dynamically tunes the output latency of an oboe::AudioStream by adjusting its buffer size based on underrun behavior. Provides tune(), requestReset(), and getters/setters for tuning parameters. It owns no resources beyond references; lifecycle of the referenced AudioStream is external.

Abstract base class that manages read/write counters and derived indices for a circular audio frame FIFO, given a fixed capacity. It exposes methods to query available frames and to advance read/write positions, while delegating storage of the monotonically increasing read/write counters to subclasses via pure virtual methods. Construction requires the total frame capacity. Destruction is trivial (virtual default).

A FIFO audio/data buffer class in the oboe namespace that manages frame-based ring storage with byte-per-frame granularity. It provides constructors for internally allocated storage or externally provided storage and shared read/write counters, plus APIs to read, write, query capacity and counters. Internals include a FifoControllerBase owner that tracks read/write positions. Full behavioral details (thread-safety, blocking semantics) are not in this header and must be inferred: operations appear non-blocking and sized in frames.

A callback adapter in the oboe namespace that wraps an existing AudioStreamCallback to stabilize callback timing/load. It forwards error callbacks to the wrapped callback and tracks frame count and timing to generate controlled CPU load via generateLoad. Exact stabilization algorithm is not shown here; details depend on the .cpp implementation.

Utility class providing static time-related helpers for nanosecond-resolution timing using POSIX clocks. It wraps clock_gettime and clock_nanosleep to obtain current time in nanoseconds and to sleep until a target time or for a duration. It relies on kNanosPerSecond from oboe/Definitions.h; destruction/ownership is irrelevant because it is a pure static utility with no instances.

A testing-only utility class in the oboe namespace that exposes static probes and controls related to AAudio MMAP selection and partial data callback support. It provides no instance state; usage is via static methods. Details of platform interaction are not defined here and may change.

A helper class that synchronizes an input oboe::AudioStream with an output oboe::AudioStream for full-duplex processing. Acts as an AudioStreamDataCallback for the output stream and internally reads from the input stream, invoking the user-implemented onBothStreamsReady to process audio. Manages startup, stop, initial draining/discarding to reach steady state, and a configurable input cushion and minimum frames threshold.
This header file only includes other Oboe headers and does not define any custom types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) itself. Therefore, there are no types to document from this file.

functions.name: oboe::OboeGlobals::areWorkaroundsEnabled
functions.description: Returns the current global flag indicating whether Oboe’s internal workarounds for AAudio/OpenSL ES issues are enabled. Use to query the process-wide setting before creating/configuring streams or when diagnosing behavior differences in tests.
requirements: No arguments.
Returns a boolean indicating the current global state.
Thread-safety is not documented; if accessed concurrently with setWorkaroundsEnabled, callers should synchronize externally.

functions.name: oboe::OboeGlobals::setWorkaroundsEnabled
functions.description: Sets the global flag controlling whether Oboe’s internal workarounds are enabled. Pass false to disable workarounds, e.g., when writing tests to reproduce underlying AAudio or OpenSL ES bugs. Affects process-wide behavior of Oboe.
requirements: Parameter enabled must be a boolean value.
This modifies global state for the process and may affect all Oboe operations created/used after the change.
Thread-safety is not documented; callers should ensure external synchronization if set from multiple threads or while other threads query the flag.

functions.name: oboe::ResultWithValue::ResultWithValue
functions.description: Constructor that creates a ResultWithValue holding an error result; the stored value is value-initialized. Use when an operation failed and no meaningful value is available.
requirements: T must be value-initializable (mValue is initialized with {}).
T must be storable as a const data member (copied or moved into the object as needed).

functions.name: oboe::ResultWithValue::error
functions.description: Returns the stored result code for this ResultWithValue instance. Use to inspect success or the specific error.

functions.name: oboe::ResultWithValue::value
functions.description: Returns the stored value by value. Typically used after checking the result is OK (e.g., via operator bool).
requirements: T must be copy-constructible (returned by value).
Callers should check that error() is oboe::Result::OK (or operator bool is true) before using the value; the class does not enforce this.

functions.name: oboe::ResultWithValue::operator bool
functions.signature: template <typename T> explicit oboe::ResultWithValue<T>::operator bool() const
functions.description: Boolean conversion that evaluates to true when the result is OK, false otherwise. Enables idiomatic condition checks on ResultWithValue.

functions.name: oboe::ResultWithValue::operator !
functions.description: Logical negation operator returning true when the result indicates an error (non-OK), false when OK. Provides a quick error check.

functions.name: oboe::ResultWithValue::operator Result
functions.description: Implicit conversion to oboe::Result for convenient comparisons or assignments to a Result. Returns the stored result code.

functions.name: oboe::ResultWithValue::createBasedOnSign
functions.description: Factory that interprets a numeric result: non-negative values yield OK with the value set to numericResult; negative values are cast to oboe::Result and represent an error (value is default-initialized). Useful when wrapping APIs that return negative error codes and non-negative success values.
requirements: T must be an arithmetic type (int or float) as enforced by static_assert.
For negative numericResult values, the cast static_cast<oboe::Result>(numericResult) must yield a meaningful oboe::Result value for the caller’s context.

functions.name: oboe::operator<<
functions.signature: template <typename T> std::ostream& oboe::operator<<(std::ostream& strm, const oboe::ResultWithValue<T>& result)

requirements: strm must be a valid std::ostream.
T must be stream-insertable into std::ostream when the result is OK.
A convertToText(oboe::Result) function must be available and linked to format error codes.

functions.description: Converts an array of 32-bit floating point audio samples to 16-bit PCM integer samples. Use when preparing float audio buffers for APIs or devices expecting PCM16. The conversion processes numSamples values from source into destination.
requirements: source must point to a readable array containing at least numSamples float elements (inferred from pointer usage and numSamples).
destination must point to a writable array containing at least numSamples int16_t elements (inferred).
numSamples must be >= 0 (inferred).
Pointers must be valid for the duration of the call and must not be null if numSamples > 0 (inferred).

requirements: source must point to a readable array containing at least numSamples int16_t elements (inferred).
destination must point to a writable array containing at least numSamples float elements (inferred).

Pointers must be valid for the duration of the call and must not be null if numSamples > 0 (inferred).

functions.name: oboe::convertFormatToSizeInBytes
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of a single audio sample for the given AudioFormat, or 0 if the format is invalid or unsupported. Useful for buffer size calculations.

functions.name: oboe::convertToText
functions.signature: template <typename FromType> const char * oboe::convertToText(FromType input)
functions.description: Returns the ASCII text symbol for the supplied Oboe enum value, or an English message indicating the value is unrecognized. Intended for developer/debug output, not for end-user display. The returned C-string does not need to be freed.
requirements: input should be an Oboe enum or type for which a convertToText specialization/overload exists (inferred from comment).

functions.name: oboe::getVersionText

Based on the surrounding definitions, this is expected to correspond to the MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH text (e.g., OBOE_VERSION_TEXT). Useful for logging or feature checks. Details about storage duration and thread-safety are not documented in this header; treat the returned pointer as a read-only, null-terminated string and copy it if a persistent, mutable buffer is needed.

The returned value should be handled as a null-terminated C-string; if a non-owning pointer is unsuitable, copy it to caller-managed storage.
No error handling or null-return behavior is specified in this header.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBase::AudioStreamBase
functions.description: Copy constructor. Creates a shallow copy of the stream configuration fields and callback pointers/shared_ptrs. The class contains only primitive values and pointer/shared_ptr fields and is safe to copy as designed.
requirements: Source object must be a valid AudioStreamBase instance.
Callbacks stored as raw pointers are copied as-is; callers must ensure pointer lifetime remains valid if they are later used.
Shared callback objects (std::shared_ptr) will have their reference counts incremented.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBase::~AudioStreamBase

requirements: Both source and destination must be valid objects.

Shared callback objects (std::shared_ptr) will be reassigned; reference counts updated accordingly.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamDataCallback::~AudioStreamDataCallback
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the AudioStreamDataCallback interface. Allows proper cleanup via base-class pointer. No operational behavior beyond default destruction.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamDataCallback::onAudioReady
functions.signature: virtual DataCallbackResult onAudioReady(AudioStream* audioStream, void* audioData, int32_t numFrames) = 0;
functions.description: Real-time audio data callback. For output streams, render and write exactly numFrames of audio in the stream’s current format into audioData. For input streams, read and process exactly numFrames from audioData. Do not call read() or write() on the stream within this callback. Intended for hard real-time processing; avoid operations that may block or add unbounded latency.
requirements: Must process exactly numFrames frames unless using the partial data callback API instead.
Must not call oboeStream->read() or oboeStream->write() from this callback.
Must not call oboeStream->stop(), pause(), flush(), or close() from this callback.
Must not allocate memory (e.g., malloc/new) inside the callback.
Must not perform file I/O operations inside the callback.
Must not perform network operations inside the callback.
Must not use mutexes or other synchronization primitives inside the callback.
Must not sleep inside the callback.
It is OK to call oboeStream->get*(), oboe::convertToText(), and oboeStream->setBufferSizeInFrames().
numFrames may vary unless AudioStreamBuilder::setFramesPerCallback() is used; if not set, numFrames <= AudioStream::getFramesPerBurst().
Return value must be DataCallbackResult::Continue to keep streaming or DataCallbackResult::Stop to stop.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamErrorCallback::~AudioStreamErrorCallback
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the AudioStreamErrorCallback interface. Enables proper cleanup via base-class pointer.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamErrorCallback::onError
functions.signature: virtual bool onError(AudioStream* audioStream, Result error);
functions.description: Early error notification invoked when a stream encounters an error (e.g., disconnection). Allows an application to override and customize normal error handling. Returning true indicates the application has already stopped and closed the stream; returning false lets Oboe perform default handling (calling onErrorBeforeClose(), then closing, then onErrorAfterClose()). Called on a thread created by Oboe.
requirements: If this method returns true, the application must stop() and close() the stream itself.
If this method returns false, Oboe will stop and close the stream and invoke onErrorBeforeClose() and onErrorAfterClose().
This method is called on a thread created by Oboe; implementation must be thread-safe.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamErrorCallback::onErrorBeforeClose
functions.signature: virtual void onErrorBeforeClose(AudioStream* audioStream, Result error);
functions.description: Error callback invoked after onError() returns false and after Oboe has stopped the stream, but before the stream is closed. You may query the stream state here. Do not close or delete the stream in this method; Oboe will close it after this callback returns. Called on a thread created by Oboe.
requirements: Called only if onError() returned false.
The underlying stream has been stopped by Oboe but not yet closed; it may be queried.
Must not close or delete the stream in this method.
This method is called on a thread created by Oboe; implementation must be thread-safe.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamErrorCallback::onErrorAfterClose
functions.signature: virtual void onErrorAfterClose(AudioStream* audioStream, Result error);
functions.description: Error callback invoked after onError() returns false and after Oboe has stopped and closed the underlying AAudio or OpenSL ES stream. You cannot reference the underlying stream, but most parameters can still be queried. Suitable for reopening a new stream (e.g., on another device).
requirements: Called only if onError() returned false.
The underlying AAudio/OpenSL ES stream has been stopped and closed by Oboe; it cannot be referenced.
Most parameters can still be queried on the AudioStream wrapper after close.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamPresentationCallback::~AudioStreamPresentationCallback
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the AudioStreamPresentationCallback interface.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamPresentationCallback::onPresentationEnded
functions.description: Notification that all queued buffers of an offloaded stream have been played by the audio system (framework + hardware). Useful for tracking end-of-stream or scheduling subsequent actions for offloaded playback.
requirements: audioStream points to the associated stream; no other explicit requirements are stated.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamPartialDataCallback::~AudioStreamPartialDataCallback
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the AudioStreamPartialDataCallback interface.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamPartialDataCallback::onPartialAudioReady
functions.signature: virtual int32_t onPartialAudioReady(AudioStream* audioStream, void* audioData, int32_t numFrames) = 0;
functions.description: Real-time partial audio data callback. Allows processing fewer than numFrames frames per invocation. For output, render and write at most numFrames frames into audioData. For input, read and process at most numFrames frames from audioData. Return the actual number of frames processed, or a negative value to stop the stream. Same real-time constraints and prohibitions as onAudioReady apply.
requirements: Return value must be in the range [0, numFrames] to indicate frames actually processed; a negative return value will stop the stream.
Must not call oboeStream->read() or oboeStream->write() from this callback.
Must not call oboeStream->stop(), pause(), flush(), or close() from this callback.
Must not allocate memory (e.g., malloc/new) inside the callback.
Must not perform file I/O operations inside the callback.
Must not perform network operations inside the callback.
Must not use mutexes or other synchronization primitives inside the callback.
Must not sleep inside the callback.
It is OK to call oboeStream->get*(), oboe::convertToText(), and oboeStream->setBufferSizeInFrames().
numFrames may vary unless AudioStreamBuilder::setFramesPerCallback() is used; if not set, numFrames <= AudioStream::getFramesPerBurst().
Android supports partial data callbacks via AAudio starting at API level 37; on devices without support, apps must process all requested data to avoid data loss.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamCallback::~AudioStreamCallback
functions.description: Virtual destructor for the combined AudioStreamCallback interface (deprecated in favor of AudioStreamDataCallback and AudioStreamErrorCallback).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::AudioStreamBuilder
functions.description: Default constructor for the AudioStreamBuilder. Initializes a new builder with default/unspecified stream attributes that can be configured via setter methods before opening a stream.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::AudioStreamBuilder
functions.description: Constructs an AudioStreamBuilder, copying base stream parameters from an existing AudioStreamBase. Allows initializing the builder with pre-existing configuration before further customization.
requirements: audioStreamBase must remain valid for the duration of this constructor call (usual reference parameter requirement).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setChannelCount
functions.description: Requests a specific channel count for the stream. Resets the channel mask to Unspecified. If left unspecified, the actual channel count should be queried from the opened stream.
requirements: channelCount may be kUnspecified to defer selection to the system.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setChannelMask
functions.description: Requests a specific channel mask for the stream. Also sets the channel count to the count implied by the mask. On Android 32+, this takes effect; on older versions it is ignored. If setChannelCount is also used, the last call wins.
requirements: channelMask may be ChannelMask::Unspecified.
Effective only on Android API level 32+; otherwise has no effect.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setDirection
functions.description: Sets the stream direction (input or output). Default is Direction::Output.
requirements: direction must be Direction::Output or Direction::Input.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setSampleRate
functions.description: Requests a specific sample rate (frames per second). If left unspecified, the actual value should be queried after opening.
requirements: sampleRate may be kUnspecified to defer selection to the system.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setFramesPerCallback
functions.description: Deprecated. Use setFramesPerDataCallback instead. Requests a specific number of frames for each data callback.
requirements: framesPerCallback may be kUnspecified to allow variable-size callbacks.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setFramesPerDataCallback
functions.description: Requests a specific number of frames per invocation of the data callback. Unspecified allows the system to choose and may vary per callback. Larger than burst size may skip some bursts; smaller may cause multiple callbacks per burst.
requirements: framesPerCallback may be kUnspecified to allow variable-size callbacks.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setFormat
functions.description: Requests a specific audio sample format (e.g., Float). If unspecified, query the stream after opening.
requirements: format may be AudioFormat::Unspecified.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setBufferCapacityInFrames
functions.description: Sets the requested buffer capacity in frames (maximum possible buffer size). Actual capacity may differ (AAudio: at least this big; OpenSL ES: may be smaller).
requirements: bufferCapacityInFrames may be kUnspecified.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::getAudioApi
functions.description: Returns the audio API that will be requested when opening the stream. The actual API used may differ; query the opened stream to confirm.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setAudioApi
functions.description: Specifies the audio API to request (Unspecified, OpenSLES, or AAudio). Usually leave unspecified to let Oboe choose at runtime.
requirements: audioApi must be AudioApi::Unspecified, AudioApi::OpenSLES, or AudioApi::AAudio.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::isAAudioSupported
functions.description: Returns whether the AAudio API is supported on the device (introduced in Android 8.0).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::isAAudioRecommended
functions.description: Returns whether AAudio is recommended on this device/SDK, accounting for version-specific issues (not recommended for Android 8.0 or earlier).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setSharingMode
functions.description: Requests a device sharing mode (Shared or Exclusive). The requested mode may not be available; check the opened stream for actual mode.
requirements: sharingMode must be SharingMode::Shared or SharingMode::Exclusive.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setPerformanceMode
functions.description: Requests a performance mode affecting latency, power consumption, and glitch protection (e.g., LowLatency).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setUsage
functions.description: Sets the intended usage for an output stream (e.g., Game). Influences system behavior like volume/focus. Ignored for input streams. Default is Usage::Media. Available since API 28.
requirements: usage applies to output streams; ignored for input.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setContentType
functions.description: Sets the content type for an output stream (e.g., Speech). Can influence behaviors like handling during notifications. Ignored for input streams. Default is ContentType::Music. Available since API 28.
requirements: contentType applies to output streams; ignored for input.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setInputPreset
functions.description: Sets the input (capture) preset to optimize recording behavior (mic selection, processing). Default is VoiceRecognition due to generally lower latency. Available since API 28.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setSessionId
functions.description: Sets the requested session ID for associating streams with effects (Java AudioEffect API). Use SessionId::Allocate to have a session allocated on open; retrieve via AudioStream::getSessionId(). Session IDs interoperate with Android Java APIs. Available since API 28.
requirements: If using SessionId::Allocate, obtain the allocated ID after opening the stream via AudioStream::getSessionId() for reuse/sharing.
Allocated session IDs are positive and nonzero (post-allocation property).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setDeviceId
functions.description: Requests routing the stream to a specific audio device by ID. If kUnspecified, the primary device is typically used. The request may not be honored; check stream->getDeviceId() after open. Ignored when using OpenSL ES.
requirements: deviceId may be kUnspecified or an ID obtained (e.g.) from Java AudioManager AudioDeviceInfo.getId().
Requested device may not be granted; verify after opening.
When OpenSL ES is used, the deviceId will be ignored and treated as kUnspecified.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setAllowedCapturePolicy
functions.description: Specifies whether audio from this stream may be captured by other apps or the system. Default is Unspecified (AAUDIO_ALLOW_CAPTURE_BY_ALL). Interacts with any app-wide capture policy (most restrictive applies). Available since API 29 (AAudio).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setPrivacySensitiveMode
functions.description: Marks an input stream as privacy sensitive or not. Enabled prevents concurrent capture. Defaults to Disabled except for certain input presets (VoiceRecognition, Camcorder). Applies only to input streams using AAudio. Available since API 30 (AAudio).
requirements: Only relevant for Direction::Input streams using AAudio; has no effect otherwise.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setIsContentSpatialized
functions.description: Indicates whether the output stream's audio content has already been spatialized, to avoid double-processing by platform spatializers. Default false. Available since API 32.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setSpatializationBehavior
functions.description: Sets the desired behavior controlling whether spatialization will be applied when supported/enabled. Default is SpatializationBehavior::Never. Available since API 32.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setDataCallback
functions.description: Sets a shared_ptr-based data callback handler for audio I/O. Holds a shared_ptr to keep the callback alive for the stream lifetime. If also setting a partial data callback, the last call wins. Prefer this for general low-latency use; for offload/compressed use cases, consider setPartialDataCallback.
requirements: Callback methods have restrictions; see AudioStreamCallback documentation.
When both setDataCallback and setPartialDataCallback are called, the callback from the last call is used.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setDataCallback
functions.description: Deprecated raw-pointer variant of setDataCallback. Does not retain ownership of the callback; the app must ensure the object remains valid while the stream uses it. If also setting a partial data callback, the last call wins.
requirements: The dataCallback object must outlive the stream usage to avoid use-after-free.
Deprecated: prefer setDataCallback(std::shared_ptr<AudioStreamDataCallback>).
When both setDataCallback and setPartialDataCallback are called, the callback from the last call is used.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setPartialDataCallback
functions.description: Sets a shared_ptr-based partial data callback handler, allowing callbacks that process a subset of provided data. Intended for offload, deep buffer, or large-buffer scenarios; not generally for low-latency small buffers. Only supported by AAudio (API 37+). If set on devices/APIs that don't support it or with OpenSLES, stream opening will fail. Last call between data and partial data callback determines which is used.
requirements: Partial data callback is supported only by AAudio and from API level 37; using it on unsupported devices will cause openStream to fail.
OpenSLES does not support partial data callbacks; using OpenSLES with this set will cause openStream to fail.
When both setPartialDataCallback and setDataCallback are called, the callback from the last call is used.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setErrorCallback
functions.description: Sets a shared_ptr-based error callback to receive disconnection and other error notifications (e.g., device changes, service failures, stolen exclusive streams). Holds a shared_ptr to keep the callback alive.
requirements: Error callbacks are invoked only when a data callback is set and the stream is started; otherwise read()/write()/requestStart() return errors directly.
Follow AudioStreamCallback threading restrictions.
When an error callback occurs, the associated stream must be stopped and closed on a separate thread.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setErrorCallback
functions.description: Deprecated raw-pointer variant of setErrorCallback. Does not retain ownership of the callback; the app must ensure the object remains valid while the stream uses it.
requirements: The errorCallback object must outlive the stream usage to avoid use-after-free.
Deprecated: prefer setErrorCallback(std::shared_ptr<AudioStreamErrorCallback>).
Error callbacks are invoked only when a data callback is set and the stream is started.
Follow AudioStreamCallback threading restrictions.
When an error callback occurs, the associated stream must be stopped and closed on a separate thread.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setPresentationCallback
functions.description: Sets a shared_ptr-based presentation callback to be notified when all queued data for an offload stream has been played. Callback is active only when a data callback is set and the stream is started.
requirements: Presentation callbacks are invoked only when a data callback is set and the stream is started.
Follow AudioStreamCallback restrictions within callback methods.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setCallback
functions.description: Deprecated convenience method to set the same raw-pointer object as both data and error callback (via dual inheritance). Resets any partial data callback. Not recommended due to raw pointer lifetime risks.
requirements: The streamCallback object must outlive the stream usage to avoid use-after-free.
Deprecated: prefer setDataCallback(std::shared_ptr<...>) and setErrorCallback(std::shared_ptr<...>) separately.
Resets any previously set partial data callback.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setChannelConversionAllowed
functions.description: Allows Oboe to perform channel count conversions to achieve optimal results on certain devices (e.g., mono/stereo fallback to access low-latency paths). Default false.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setFormatConversionAllowed
functions.description: Allows Oboe to perform sample format conversions to obtain optimal paths (e.g., open I16 and convert to float). Default false.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setSampleRateConversionQuality
functions.description: Sets the quality level of Oboe's sample rate converter. None disables Oboe SRC (underlying APIs may still resample). Default is Medium. Performing SRC in Oboe can preserve low-latency paths.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setPackageName
functions.description: Declares the package name of the app creating the stream (usually Context#getPackageName()). Required by some input streams for permission checks. Available since API 31.
requirements: Provide a valid package name; invalid names may cause input stream permission failures when starting.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::setAttributionTag
functions.description: Declares the attribution tag associated with the context creating the stream (usually Context#getAttributionTag()). Default is null. Available since API 31.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::willUseAAudio
functions.description: Returns true if, based on current builder settings and device capabilities, Oboe will use AAudio (requested and supported, or unspecified and recommended).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::openStream
functions.description: Creates and opens an AudioStream based on the builder settings. The caller receives ownership of the raw pointer and must close/delete the stream when done. Deprecated in favor of the shared_ptr version.
requirements: stream must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the created AudioStream*.
The caller is responsible for closing and deleting the returned stream.
Deprecated: prefer openStream(std::shared_ptr<oboe::AudioStream>&).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::openStream
functions.description: Creates and opens an AudioStream based on the builder settings, returning it via a shared_ptr. Oboe uses the shared_ptr internally to prevent deletion while callbacks are active.
requirements: stream must be a valid reference to a shared_ptr that will receive the created stream.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStreamBuilder::openManagedStream
functions.description: Creates and opens a ManagedStream (unique_ptr with a custom deleter) based on the builder settings. The unique_ptr will automatically close and delete the stream when it goes out of scope. Deprecated in favor of the shared_ptr openStream.
requirements: stream must be a valid reference to a ManagedStream (std::unique_ptr<AudioStream, StreamDeleterFunctor>).
Deprecated: prefer openStream(std::shared_ptr<oboe::AudioStream>&).

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::AudioStream
functions.description: Default constructor for an Oboe AudioStream base object. Initializes internal counters and state to defaults. Typically constructed via AudioStreamBuilder and not used directly by apps.
requirements: Intended for framework/internal use; applications normally create streams via oboe::AudioStreamBuilder.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::~AudioStream
functions.description: Virtual destructor for AudioStream. Ensures proper cleanup in subclasses when a stream object is destroyed.
requirements: If a stream is open, callers should call close() before destruction to free resources as recommended by Oboe documentation.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::open
functions.description: Opens the stream based on the current settings. Base implementation returns Result::OK and is meant to be overridden by subclasses.
requirements: Should be called before I/O operations (read/write) or state changes (start/pause/stop).
Not recommended to re-open a stream that has been closed.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::release
functions.description: Releases audio resources associated with the stream without fully closing it, allowing concurrent queries from other threads. Fully implemented only for MMAP streams; on legacy streams some resources/callbacks may linger. Available from AAudio API level 30; returns ErrorUnimplemented otherwise.
requirements: Callers should subsequently call close() at some point after release().
After calling, the stream enters AAUDIO_STREAM_STATE_CLOSING.
Do not rely on complete teardown on legacy (non-MMAP) paths; some callbacks may still occur.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::close
functions.description: Closes the stream and deallocates resources from open(). May sleep briefly before closing to avoid races with callbacks.
requirements: Should be called when the stream is no longer needed.
Avoid calling from within callbacks; see notes on potential post-close callbacks and delay-before-close behavior.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::start
functions.description: Starts the stream, blocking until started, an error occurs, or the timeout elapses.
requirements: May block up to timeoutNanoseconds; a value of 0 implies a non-blocking start attempt.
Should be called on a successfully opened stream.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::pause
functions.description: Pauses the stream, blocking until paused, an error occurs, or the timeout elapses.
requirements: May block up to timeoutNanoseconds; 0 implies non-blocking.
Call only on streams that support pausing and are in a state that can transition to paused.

functions.name: oboe::AudioStream::flush
functions.description: Flushes the stream, blocking until flushed, an error occurs, or the timeout elapses.
requirements: May block up to timeoutNanoseconds; 0 implies non-blocking.

functions.description: Architecture-specific macro that emits a minimal instruction to hint the CPU to relax/yield during busy-wait loops. On x86 it expands to "rep; nop"; on AArch64 to "yield"; on ARM/MIPS/RISC-V to an empty memory clobber. If none of the supported architectures are detected at compile time, compilation fails.
requirements: Only available when compiling for one of: __i386__, __x86_64__, __arm__, __mips__, __riscv, or __aarch64__; otherwise a compile-time error is triggered.
Takes no arguments and returns no value; intended for use within spin-wait/busy-wait code paths.
Because it is a macro emitting inline assembly, it should only be used in contexts where such assembly is permitted by the toolchain and optimization settings.

functions.name: oboe::AudioClock::getNanoseconds
functions.description: Returns the current time from the specified POSIX clock as a 64-bit count of nanoseconds. Internally calls clock_gettime(clockId, ...) and converts timespec to nanoseconds using kNanosPerSecond (defined in oboe/Definitions.h). If clock_gettime fails, the negative errno-style result from clock_gettime is returned. Typical usage: capture a monotonic timestamp for scheduling or measuring intervals.
requirements: clockId must be a valid POSIX clock supported by clock_gettime (e.g., CLOCK_MONOTONIC by default).
Caller must handle negative return values as error conditions from clock_gettime.
Returned value is an absolute time in nanoseconds for the chosen clock domain.

functions.name: oboe::AudioClock::sleepUntilNanoTime
functions.signature: static int oboe::AudioClock::sleepUntilNanoTime(int64_t nanoTime, clockid_t clockId = CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
functions.description: Sleeps the calling thread until the absolute time nanoTime (in nanoseconds) on the specified clock. Uses clock_nanosleep with TIMER_ABSTIME. Returns 0 on success, or a negative errno-style value (e.g., -EINTR) if interrupted or on error. Use this to block until a target time point in the given clock domain.
requirements: nanoTime is an absolute time in nanoseconds for the given clockId (not a relative duration).
clockId must be a POSIX clock supported by clock_nanosleep for absolute sleeps (default CLOCK_MONOTONIC).
Caller must handle negative return values (e.g., -EINTR on signal interrupt).
Behavior if nanoTime represents a time in the past is determined by clock_nanosleep; caller should be prepared for immediate return or an error per platform semantics.

functions.name: oboe::AudioClock::sleepForNanos
functions.signature: static int oboe::AudioClock::sleepForNanos(int64_t nanoseconds, clockid_t clockId = CLOCK_REALTIME)
functions.description: Sleeps the calling thread for a relative duration of nanoseconds on the specified clock. If nanoseconds is negative, returns immediately with 0. Otherwise uses clock_nanosleep for a relative sleep. Returns 0 on success, or a negative errno-style value (e.g., -EINTR) if interrupted or on error. Use this to delay execution by a relative interval.
requirements: If nanoseconds < 0, the function returns immediately with 0 and performs no sleep.
For nanoseconds > 0, the value is treated as a relative duration in nanoseconds.
clockId must be a POSIX clock supported by clock_nanosleep for relative sleeps (default CLOCK_REALTIME).
Caller must handle negative return values (e.g., -EINTR on signal interrupt).

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::setSharedInputStream

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::getInputStream

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::setSharedOutputStream

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::getOutputStream
functions.description: Returns the current output AudioStream pointer. If a shared output stream has been set, its raw pointer is returned; otherwise the raw pointer set via setOutputStream is returned. May return nullptr if no stream has been set.
requirements: None. Caller must handle a nullptr return.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::start
functions.description: Starts full-duplex operation by requesting start on the input stream and then on the output stream. Allocates/expands an internal float input buffer sized for the worst-case callback load based on the output stream’s capacity and channel count. Initializes internal counters for drain/cushion/discard phases.
requirements: Must call setInputStream/setSharedInputStream and setOutputStream/setSharedOutputStream prior to start(); both streams must be non-null.
Both streams must be opened successfully before start(); the method calls requestStart() on each.
The output stream should have this FullDuplexStream instance set as its data callback (via setDataCallback) before starting, so onAudioReady can drive processing.
On failure of input requestStart(), the function returns that error and does not start the output stream.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::stop
functions.description: Requests stop on the output stream (if present) and then on the input stream (if present). Returns Result::OK only if neither stop request reports an error; otherwise returns the first non-OK result (prefers output result if it failed).
requirements: May be called even if one or both streams are nullptr; those calls are skipped.
Caller is responsible for closing both streams after stopping, per class-level documentation.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::readInput
functions.description: Reads up to numFrames from the input stream into the internally managed float buffer (mInputBuffer). Intended to be called by onAudioReady during duplex processing.
requirements: Caller should not call this directly; it is intended to be invoked from onAudioReady().
getInputStream() must return a valid stream; otherwise read will fail.
mInputBuffer must be allocated large enough to hold the requested frames; start() prepares/expands this buffer.
Timeout is fixed at 0 (non-blocking) within this function.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::onBothStreamsReady
functions.signature: virtual oboe::DataCallbackResult onBothStreamsReady(const void *inputData, int numInputFrames, void *outputData, int numOutputFrames) = 0
functions.description: User-implemented callback invoked when both input data and output processing are ready. Provides readable inputData/numInputFrames and a writable outputData/numOutputFrames to produce output. Must return Continue to keep streaming or Stop to halt.
requirements: Must be overridden by subclasses; this is a pure virtual function.
inputData may be nullptr and/or numInputFrames may be zero; implementation must handle these cases.
numOutputFrames may be zero; implementation must handle this case.
If returning Stop, the input stream will be requested to stop by the framework.
Implementation should write up to numOutputFrames of valid audio to outputData when continuing.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::onAudioReady
functions.description: Output stream data callback that coordinates duplex I/O. It clears the output buffer, manages a drain/cushion/discard sequence to synchronize with the input stream, performs non-blocking reads from the input, then calls onBothStreamsReady with the available input frames and output buffer. If errors occur or Stop is requested, it stops the input stream.
requirements: Should be registered as the data callback of the output stream via setDataCallback(this).
audioData must point to a writable buffer for numFrames frames as provided by the output stream callback.
Relies on both input and output streams being valid and started (start() sets up internal state).
Caller must have implemented onBothStreamsReady(); this function invokes it and propagates its Continue/Stop result.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::setNumInputBurstsCushion
functions.description: Sets the number of input bursts to leave in the input buffer as a cushion between DSP and app processor cursors to reduce collisions. Typical values: 0 for latency measurement, 1 for glitch tests.
requirements: numBursts is an application-chosen integer; no explicit range constraints are stated.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::getNumInputBurstsCushion
functions.description: Returns the configured number of input bursts to retain as a cushion in the input buffer.
requirements: None.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::setMinimumFramesBeforeRead
functions.description: Sets the minimum number of frames that must be available in the input stream before readInput() will be attempted during processing.
requirements: numFrames is an application-chosen integer; no explicit range constraints are stated.

functions.name: oboe::FullDuplexStream::getMinimumFramesBeforeRead
functions.description: Returns the minimum number of input frames required before readInput() is attempted.
requirements: None.

import random
import string

# Data type: package name string
# - Non-empty
# - Typically dot-separated tokens (labels)
# - Labels: start with letter, then letters/digits/underscore; avoid spaces
# - Reasonable length (fuzzer trims to 128). Keep total <= 128 bytes.
# - ASCII/UTF-8 safe
# This generator creates varied but valid Android-like package names.

RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL = [
    "com", "org", "net", "io", "app", "dev", "edu", "gov"
]

COMMON_VENDORS = [
    "google", "android", "example", "sample", "demo", "test", "fuzz",
    "vendor", "acme", "contoso", "examplecorp", "widgets"
]

COMMON_APPS = [
    "app", "music", "camera", "game", "chat", "maps", "player",
    "recorder", "notebook", "gallery", "launcher", "service",
    "provider", "daemon", "client", "server"
]

ALPHA = string.ascii_lowercase
ALNUM_UNDERSCORE = ALPHA + string.digits + "_"


def _rand_label(rng: random.Random, min_len: int = 1, max_len: int = 24) -> str:
    # Start with a letter to mimic Java package label rules
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    first = rng.choice(ALPHA)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(ALNUM_UNDERSCORE) for _ in range(max(0, length - 1)))
    return first + rest


def _compose_package(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Decide style
    style = rng.choice(["reserved.vendor.app", "reserved.random.app", "random.random.app",
                        "reverse_dns_depth4", "short_two", "long_chain"])

    labels = []
    if style == "reserved.vendor.app":
        labels.append(rng.choice(RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL))
        labels.append(rng.choice(COMMON_VENDORS))
        labels.append(rng.choice(COMMON_APPS))
    elif style == "reserved.random.app":
        labels.append(rng.choice(RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL))
        labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 3, 12))
        labels.append(rng.choice(COMMON_APPS))
    elif style == "random.random.app":
        labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 2, 6))
        labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 3, 10))
        labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 3, 12))
    elif style == "reverse_dns_depth4":
        labels.append(rng.choice(RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL))
        labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 3, 10))
        labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 3, 10))
        labels.append(rng.choice(COMMON_APPS))
    elif style == "short_two":
        labels.append(rng.choice(RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL))
        labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 2, 8))
    elif style == "long_chain":
        depth = rng.randint(4, 7)
        labels.append(rng.choice(RESERVED_TOP_LEVEL))
        for _ in range(depth - 1):
            labels.append(_rand_label(rng, 2, 10))

    # Optionally insert numeric flavor or underscore suffixes in middle labels
    for i in range(1, len(labels) - 1):
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            # append a numeric version tag or underscore token
            tag = rng.choice([str(rng.randint(1, 999)), f"_{rng.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz')}" ])
            labels[i] = (labels[i] + tag)[:24]

    pkg = ".".join(labels)

    # Ensure length within 128; if too long, trim last label appropriately
    if len(pkg) > 128:
        over = len(pkg) - 128
        parts = pkg.split('.')
        if parts:
            last = parts[-1]
            if len(last) > over:
                parts[-1] = last[:-over]
            else:
                # fallback: trim to 128 total
                pkg = pkg[:128]
                # remove trailing dot if any
                if pkg.endswith('.'):
                    pkg = pkg[:-1]
                return pkg
        pkg = ".".join(parts)

    # Final guard: non-empty and no spaces
    pkg = pkg.strip().replace(' ', '.')
    if not pkg:
        pkg = "com.example.app"
    return pkg


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally generate some well-known canonical values
    canonical = [
        "com.example.app",
        "com.google.android",
        "org.example.demo",
        "io.app.test",
        "dev.fuzz.player",
    ]
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        pkg = rng.choice(canonical)
    else:
        pkg = _compose_package(rng)

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes; ensure <= 4096 (guaranteed by construction)
    data = pkg.encode('utf-8')
    return data[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: attribution tag string
# Requirements from stub:
# - Non-empty UTF-8 string
# - Kept short (<=64 bytes)
# - Free-form; interesting coverage via different classes
# - Must not contain NULs in source or output

# Character blocks for composing tags (no NULs)
UNICODE_BLOCKS: List[str] = [
    string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.",
    "!@#$%^&*()-_=+[]{};:',.<>/?|~`",
    " \t",
    "😀😃😄😁😆😉😊😍😘😜🤔👍🔥✨🎵🎮📱🧪",
    "áàäâãåçéèëêíìïîñóòöôõúùüûÿžßœøåÅÆæÞþÐð",
    "\u0301\u0300\u0302\u0327\u0332\u20DD",
    "测试標籤标签タグ",
]

# Structured templates that may exercise parsing branches
SPECIAL_TEMPLATES = [
    "app:feature:%RAND%",
    "module/%RAND%",
    "com.example.%RAND%",
    "game-%RAND%-tag",
    "audio:%RAND%:latency",
    "pkg.%RAND%.attr",
]

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-_."


def _rand_from_blocks(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    s_chars: List[str] = []
    current = ""
    while len(current.encode("utf-8")) < length:
        block = rng.choice(UNICODE_BLOCKS)
        ch = rng.choice(block)
        # Avoid control characters just in case
        if ord(ch) < 32:
            continue
        tentative = (current + ch).encode("utf-8")
        if len(tentative) <= length:
            current += ch
        else:
            # try a single-byte fallback
            fb = rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII)
            if len((current + fb).encode("utf-8")) <= length:
                current += fb
            else:
                break
    return current


def _make_template(rng: random.Random, max_len: int) -> str:
    tmpl = rng.choice(SPECIAL_TEMPLATES)
    # Size of random segment chosen to likely fit
    base_len = len(tmpl) - len("%RAND%")
    avail = max(1, max_len - base_len)
    seg_len = rng.randint(3, min(16, avail))
    seg = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits) for _ in range(seg_len))
    s = tmpl.replace("%RAND%", seg)
    b = s.encode("utf-8")
    if len(b) > max_len:
        # Trim to valid UTF-8 within bound
        b = b[:max_len]
        while True:
            try:
                s = b.decode("utf-8")
                break
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                b = b[:-1]
    return s


def _biased_length(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    choices = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 63, 64]
    weights = [6, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 3, 3, 3, 3, 2, 2, 2]
    return rng.choices(choices, weights=weights, k=1)[0]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    max_bytes = 64

    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.35:
        n = _biased_length(rng)
        n = max(1, min(max_bytes, n))
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_ASCII) for _ in range(n))
    elif mode < 0.6:
        s = _make_template(rng, max_bytes)
    else:
        target = _biased_length(rng)
        target = max(1, min(max_bytes, target))
        s = _rand_from_blocks(rng, target)
        # Optionally add a combining mark if it fits
        if s and rng.random() < 0.3:
            cm = rng.choice(["\u0301", "\u0332", "\u20DD"])  # combining acute/underline/enclosing
            tentative = (s + cm).encode("utf-8")
            if len(tentative) <= max_bytes:
                s = s + cm

    if not s:
        s = "a"

    b = s.encode("utf-8")
    if len(b) > max_bytes:
        b = b[:max_bytes]
        # Fix to valid UTF-8
        while True:
            try:
                _ = b.decode("utf-8")
                break
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                b = b[:-1]

    # Avoid all-whitespace strings
    try:
        if b.decode("utf-8").strip() == "":
            b = b"tag"
    except UnicodeDecodeError:
        b = b"tag"

    return b

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: debug name string (UTF-8), short, null-terminated by fuzzer infra when using std::string.
# Fuzzer stubs call FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to obtain a std::string used as a debug tag for
# AudioStream::notifyWorkloadIncrease/Reset/Spike. We should provide interesting, valid tags.
# Strategy: generate a variety of ASCII/UTF-8 friendly names, including:
# - Short identifiers
# - Names with CPU/GPU hints, numbers, punctuation
# - Varying lengths including empty and near typical limits (~64-256 chars)
# - Include Unicode characters to exercise UTF-8 handling
# The returned bytes are consumed by the fuzzing framework which will split them for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR
# calls; thus we concatenate multiple strings separated by newlines. The harness typically reads sequentially.

UNICODE_SAMPLES = [
    "Δ", "✓", "𝛑", "😀", "音", "スペース", "тест", "اختبار", "προβα", "π", "ø", "ç", "ñ",
]

ALPHABET = string.ascii_letters + string.digits
PUNCT = "-_./:@#[](){}+,=~!$%^&"  # safe punctuation


def _rand_word(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    chars = ALPHABET + PUNCT
    return ''.join(rng.choice(chars) for _ in range(n))


def _tag_variants(rng: random.Random) -> List[str]:
    tags: List[str] = []

    # Some fixed canonical tags
    tags.extend([
        "audio", "callback", "render", "read", "write", "lowlatency", "offload",
        "cpu", "gpu", "both", "none", " spike ", " reset ", " increase ",
        "perf", "hint", "AAudio", "OpenSLES", "duplex", "Oboe",
        "",  # empty string
    ])

    # Short identifiers with indices
    for i in range(rng.randint(3, 8)):
        tags.append(f"tag{i}")

    # Words with separators and timestamps-like patterns
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        tags.append(f"work-{_rand_word(rng, 3, 8)}")
        tags.append(f"gpu:{rng.randint(0,100)}")
        tags.append(f"cpu:{rng.randint(0,100)}")

    # Longer descriptive tags
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        part1 = _rand_word(rng, 4, 10)
        part2 = _rand_word(rng, 4, 10)
        part3 = _rand_word(rng, 2, 6)
        tags.append(f"{part1}/{part2}:{part3}")

    # Include some Unicode variants
    for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 6)):
        base = _rand_word(rng, 3, 8)
        u = rng.choice(UNICODE_SAMPLES)
        where = rng.randint(0, 2)
        if where == 0:
            s = u + base
        elif where == 1:
            s = base + u
        else:
            s = base + u + _rand_word(rng, 2, 5)
        tags.append(s)

    # Variable length extremes
    tags.append(_rand_word(rng, 1, 1))  # single char
    tags.append(_rand_word(rng, 32, 48))
    tags.append(_rand_word(rng, 120, 180))

    # Deduplicate while preserving order
    seen = set()
    uniq: List[str] = []
    for t in tags:
        if t not in seen:
            seen.add(t)
            uniq.append(t)
    return uniq


def _assemble_buffer(tags: List[str], max_bytes: int = 4096) -> bytes:
    # Join with newlines so successive FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls can consume segments.
    # Ensure we do not exceed max_bytes.
    out_parts: List[bytes] = []
    total = 0
    for t in tags:
        b = t.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
        # add newline separator
        b += b"\n"
        if total + len(b) > max_bytes:
            break
        out_parts.append(b)
        total += len(b)
    return b"".join(out_parts)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    tags = _tag_variants(rng)
    rng.shuffle(tags)
    return _assemble_buffer(tags)
